guitar.notes: Steve Cropper is famous for his Fender Telecaster/Esquire ("Stax" sound), well documented.

tone.target: clean, swampy Hammond-like guitar twang with slight grit
tone.profile: clean, swampy Hammond-like guitar twang with slight grit
tone.summary: A tight signal chain using a pre-amp boost for initial tone shaping, followed by the US Deluxe amp model paired with a 2x12 cabinet to achieve a bright, percussive, swampy twang.

rig.name: Booker T. & The Mg's - Green Onions Remaster - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain tight riff articulation.
Provide slight initial grit and boost the signal for better definition without adding excessive gain.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used to simulate a clean, non-coloration tone booster (like an early clean overdrive) rather than a traditional dirt pedal.

blocks.purpose: Keep the signal clean and focused on natural guitar tone.
Simulate the bright, clean, and slightly overdriven sound of a Fender-style small combo amp.
Provide a bright, focused, and tight sound characteristic of smaller American cabinets.
Enhance the bright single-note twang and cut excessive low end to maintain tightness.
Keep the tone static and focused on percussive riffing.
Avoid lush or distracting effects like chorus.
Used only for subtle rhythmic echo if needed, otherwise kept off to maintain dryness.
blocks.gap: The primary goal is dry staccato, so this module is generally bypassed but included as a potential utility block.

blocks.purpose: Minimal ambience to prevent the sound from being too sterile, but kept low to maintain dryness.
blocks.gap: The verdict explicitly asks for 'dry staccato,' so this is used minimally or bypassed entirely.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and tonal focus for a tighter, swampy twang.

proposals.reason: Enhance the vintage Fender-style character and tightness of the tone.
proposals.expectedGain: Tighter low end, more defined upper harmonics
